transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood CSM); Dr. Maya Singh (CTO, Aurelia), Evan Brooks (Platform Lead), Rita Coleman (Procurement)

[00:00] Alex Moreno: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda: align success criteria for the POC, confirm what workload sample you'll share, go over benchmarks and then talk pilot credits and procurement path. if that sounds good?

[00:18] Dr. Maya Singh: yes thanks Alex. we're mainly focused on response latency for interactive doc summarization, and cost per consultation at scale. also security is non-negotiable — we need audit logs and KMS integration.

[00:34] Alex Moreno: understood. priya will you take the benchmarks portion?

[00:38] Priya Desai: yeah. so recommended approach: we run three benchmarks — 1) p95 latency for our median prompt sizes, 2) sustained throughput at your target rps, and 3) quality/regression checks vs your golden prompts. we'll include quantization profiles (fp16, int8-like) and measure cost per 1k tokens.

[00:55] Evan Brooks: quick q — our typical session is multi-turn, avg 220 tokens per turn, about 6 turns per session, peak 120 rps. is that something you can simulate?

[01:10] Priya Desai: yes, please send a representative one-week scrape: timestamps, prompt lengths, tokenization if possible. we'll anonymize everything on our side. note: the benchmark will model both cold and warm KV-cache scenarios.

[01:31] Rita Coleman: on the commercial side, we have a fixed pilot budget. want to know how credits will map to spend and what happens if we exceed them. also need clear exit criteria before we move to procurement.

[01:48] Alex Moreno: totally — our usual pilot guardrail is a fixed credit pool that covers run costs for the canonical benchmark suite plus a small cushion for ad-hoc tests. credits are applied to hosted usage; for private/dedicated we price differently. if we see high run rate we'll pause and alert you — no surprise overage.

[02:05] Dr. Maya Singh: can you give an example calc for our workload?

[02:10] Priya Desai: rough example — using a 13B model, fp16, with your avg session profile: estimate 0.9 USD per 1k input+output tokens on hosted but depends on batching. for a 4-week benchmark with simulated 100 rps sustained window we'll estimate somewhere in the low tens of thousands in cloud cost; we'll provide a detailed table.

[02:35] Evan Brooks: low tens of thousands is a big range. for procurement I need a concrete credit number to put in the request.

[02:40] Alex Moreno: fair. action for us: Priya and I will produce a credit model with three tiers — conservative, expected, and aggressive — and map to run counts. we'll send that by Friday.

[02:56] [speaker unclear] Jordan Li: also, on data handling — Redwood hosted keeps audit logs and supports customer-managed KMS. for Private we can do VPC deployment and on-prem options if needed; that will affect cost and procurement timeline.

[03:18] Rita Coleman: procurement will need the pilot T&Cs: liability limit, IP, data usage, termination. is there a standard pilot SOW you send?

[03:28] Alex Moreno: yes, we'll share a pilot SOW + standard T&Cs. typical pilots are 4 weeks with a single credit bucket and an acceptance test based on the success criteria we agree on.

[03:45] Dr. Maya Singh: success criteria here: p95 latency < 350ms for interactive prompts, end-to-end throughput meeting 80% of target rps with <5% error rate, and quality benchmark (ROUGE/accuracy or manual sample pass) above our current baseline. if those are met, we move to procurement.

[04:12] Priya Desai: can you confirm baseline numbers? What is current p95 and quality?

[04:18] Dr. Maya Singh: current p95 is about 520ms on our self-hosted 8xA100 setup; quality baseline F1 is 0.78 on our evaluation set.

[04:30] Priya Desai: ok that helps. we'll also capture cold start behavior — sometimes warm-cache numbers look great but cold-first-token latency spikes. we'll include both.

[04:45] Evan Brooks: about the procurement path — if POC passes, how long to get to contract and dedicated capacity?

[04:50] Alex Moreno: typical pathway: pilot -> exec sign-off -> procurement starts. timeline varies: if standard terms, 4–6 weeks; for Private deployments with SOC2 add-ons can be 8–12 weeks. we'll loop in our sales ops and legal early.

[05:10] Rita Coleman: we have internal constraints: any pilot spend above $75k requires a director-level approval. can you target credit ask within that?

[05:18] Alex Moreno: yes we'll aim for three options: 50k, 75k, 110k credits with corresponding benchmark coverage. remember credits map to run-hours on hosted; we'll show the mapping. no surprise overages and we set alerts at 60% and 85%.

[05:35] [00:05:35] Priya Desai: technical note: depending on model size selection we may recommend a warm-prefill or KV caching to match your multi-turn pattern — that materially reduces cost. we'll show cost delta in the proposal.

[06:00] Evan Brooks: are you able to run a small on-prem smoke test to validate network egress and latency? there's a strict firewall so hosted might behave differently.

[06:12] Priya Desai: yes we can do a lightweight dedicated run behind your VPC edge using a test image; that requires a short access window and minimal config — we'll include runbook. for the POC, most customers do hosted first then move to a dedicated smoke if networking is a concern.

[06:38] Dr. Maya Singh: about data privacy — we need clarity on retention and logs. our security team will review SOC2 reports and KMS flow.

[06:50] Jordan Li: noted — I'll attach SOC2 type II summary and our KMS integration guide in the follow-up.

[07:02] Rita Coleman: procurement will also want a clear acceptance test statement. can you propose a short checklist?

[07:08] Alex Moreno: yes draft acceptance checklist: 1) p95 latency target met on canonical prompts, 2) throughput target sustained for 10 minutes, 3) quality baseline pass on 500 eval prompts, 4) logs and KMS verified. we can refine with your team.

[07:26] [07:26] Dr. Maya Singh: that sounds reasonable. one more: we want to avoid vendor lock-in — what model portability or export options exist?

[07:34] Priya Desai: Redwood supports model version pinning and export of KV cache snapshots; for Private deployments you retain artifacts. we'll include a short doc.

[07:46] Evan Brooks: timeline recap: you're proposing to run benchmarks the week of 5/26; can we get preliminary numbers within 48 hours after runs?

[07:55] Priya Desai: yes, we'll aim for an initial report within 48 hours and a full write-up within 5 business days.

[08:05] Rita Coleman: procurement follow-up — what contracting team will we engage for pilot T&Cs?

[08:10] Alex Moreno: our sales ops handles pilot SOW and Redwood legal will provide a short T&Cs addendum for pilots. I'll copy both on the follow-up.

[08:22] Evan Brooks: competitor question: we ran a small eval with Anthropic and saw consistent but more expensive latency. how do you compare on cost/latency?

[08:30] Priya Desai: it depends on model/precision; Redwood's recommendable models with our runtime tend to give better throughput per dollar due to batching and KV cache; we'll include comparative numbers against open benchmarks but we can't replicate other vendors' internal pricing exactly.

[08:50] [08:50] Dr. Maya Singh: ok. anything else on success metrics?

[08:56] Alex Moreno: one more — define "quality pass" method: automated metrics + 20 manual spot checks by your SMEs; both must be satisfied.

[09:10] Evan Brooks: agreed.

[09:15] Alex Moreno: recap of next steps: Redwood to send pilot proposal + three-credit tiers and SOW by 2025-05-16; customer to send workload sample by 2025-05-20; Redwood runs benchmarks week of 2025-05-26 and provides initial results within 48 hours. procurement will start after acceptance criteria are agreed.

[09:40] Dr. Maya Singh: sounds good, thanks everyone.

[09:45] Alex Moreno: thanks all — we'll follow up in email.

[57:40] [end notes] brief crosstalk, some lines dropped mid-sentence earlier due to connectivity issue; Jordan will attach SOC2 and KMS doc in follow-up.

References mentioned: pilot SOW (link to be sent), benchmark runbook (will be attached), SOC2 summary, KMS integration guide, sample credit mapping spreadsheet.
